MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 11, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:03 p.m., on January 11, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on January 6, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation to Former Mayor Kelley

  Mayor Bucknum virtually presented former Mayor Kelley the gavel plaque.
City Council Minutes  1  January 11, 2022
 P2. Opening Remarks by Mayor Bucknum

  Received opening remarks.

P3. Recognize DryMaster on their Support of Mission Hospital

  Presented certificate of commendation.

P4. Proclaim January 2022 to be Sex Trafficking Awareness Month

  Presented proclamation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Stephanie Ming, M.V.: Spoke about her concerns with seven to eight nursing homes, vacation
rentals, and sober living homes in her neighborhood and what the city can do with the problem.

Mike Schlesinger, M.V.: Announced that he is formally requesting the Attorney General of the
State of California to authorize the filing of a lawsuit against Wendy Bucknum, Ed Sachs, and
Greg Raths to remove them from office because they have remained in office beyond the two-
term for which they were elected in 2018.

Walt Lawson M.V.: Complained on the timeline of the district mapping process and asked that
the maps be made public by January 14 so that members of the community can review them
before the January 25 Public Hearing.

Kristen Reyes M.V: Questioned if anyone will be responding to the public comments. She stated
that the detox homes within the community are very concerning and that action needs to be taken.

Mayor Bucknum stated that the City is aware of what is going on with the sober living homes and
will be holding a Town Hall Meeting and to email the City Clerk as she is keeping a list of
interested residents on this subject.

City Attorney Bill Curley stated that staff is happy to meet or call with residents regarding this,
and that there are limitations the city can do based on the State laws.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes
City Council Minutes  2  January 11, 2022
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of December 14, 2021.

2.  Check Register Dated December 3, 2021 in the Amount of $3,177,341.78

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated December 10, 2021 in the Amount of $2,830,319.06

6.  Citywide 2022 Pavement Management Program Update

  Approved a Purchase Order with Nichols Consulting Engineers, CHTD. for the 2022 update

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

  and Update Posting of FPPC Form 806 Online

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
City Council Minutes  3  January 11, 2022

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Wilberg thanked the Council for having the meeting in Zoom format this evening.
He stated that the City has about twenty employees out with COVID and another half a dozen to a
dozen that are quarantining. What this means to the public, is that we are struggling to keep our
recreation centers open so we are cutting hours, along with the Library as well.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Council Minutes  4  January 11, 2022
 City Attorney Bill Curly we are happy to report we have six maps submitted for consideration for
districting. In August we laid out a process and timeline that is consistent with the new law the Fair
Map Law. He stated that Map A was prepared by the demographer, on census data only, carefully
we made sure they did not know where Council Members lives. They did not do it to find a way to
preserve an incumbent or to allocate districts in a certain way. It is pure statistics and science. He
stated that if people choose not to believe it there is nothing we can do. He really hopes this myth
dies out because it is completely wrong and misleading and not fair to taint the community. We
will be bringing forward the maps stated in the timeline. Attorney Curley stressed that nobody was
shorted on time or opportunity, and if one felt that way it was due to not pursuing all opportunities
available to them. Stated that the Council will be to analyze and review in a public process very
transparent. Lastly, he announced that the City received a courtesy copy of a lawsuit late in the
day. After a very quick review of it, there are some substantial problems with the allegations and it
will play out in the normal course. He stressed that the governance of Mission Viejo is not at risk.
He clarified per Mayor Bucknum, that the demographer map does not have each Council Member
in their own district, in fact there is one unallocated district and two Council Members in the same
district.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he was appointed by the Orange County Transportation
Authority(OCTA) to represent them on the Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG). He
stated that he missed the first lap kick-off of the Relay 4 life. Lastly, stated he looks forward to
returning to the Council Chamber soon.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulated Mayor Bucknum. Stated that she recently had COVID and
is feeling fine now. She noted that on the Oso Creek Trail crews are cutting down brush and it’s
really looking good and indicated the hardest part was trying to find a test. She thanked the
presenters on Human Trafficking and the awareness it brought. Lastly, she also expressed that she
looks forward to returning to the Council Chamber.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths concurred that the City should be proactive on identifying testing sights
especially as this new variant is spreading around our community. He stated that his son-in-law
and daughter have COVID and he had nowhere to go and get tested. Council Member Raths
expressed his disappointment that he was not asked to be on any boards and was removed from
some other boards.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
City Council Minutes  5  January 11, 2022
 Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked the Mayor on muddling through the first meeting of the new year
and thanked staff for putting together the Zoom meeting on such short notice. He sent a shout out
to both our Chief of Police and Fire Chief for speed recoveries on their recent accidents. Expressed
that he had a wonderful time on his cross-country trip to visit family over the holiday’s and stated
that our Country is filled with genuine heroes and people who love this Country and it was great
seeing them. Lastly, he stated he looks forward to this new year

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum shared that she attended and Orange County Council of Governments event in
mid-December along with an event with the Mission Viejo Nadadores at the Oso Creek Golf
Course. She attended the first lap for the Relay 4 Life kick off. It was symbolic world-wide lap.
Steve Bell and the Relay 4 Life Team will give a presentation in February. The event will take
place April 2 at the Norman P. Community Center and asked that residents put this on their radar.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:24 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 25, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
